description: The biggest oak in California: 15-30 m tall, with a massive grey trunk, a broad dome of long limbs whose outer branches droop toward the ground, and deeply lobed leaves with rounded lobes. It grows on deep soils of the valley floors and lower slopes, where its roots reach the water table, and its long acorns feed deer, squirrels, jays, woodpeckers and wild turkeys.

season_notes.winter: Bare: the great grey limbs and the hanging tips of the outer branches show, with green balls of mistletoe high in the crown.
season_notes.spring: Leaves come out pale green in March with hanging catkins; this year's acorns start on the new shoots.
season_notes.summer: In full dark green leaf, the deepest shade in the valley; the long acorns grow through the summer.
season_notes.fall: The long acorns ripen and drop (September-November) and the leaves turn yellow-brown before falling.

notes: Valley oak is the largest North American oak: usually 10-25 m (FEIS), here 15-25 m in the file with a veteran class to 30 m, dbh 0.5-0.7 m commonly and well over 1.5 m on old trees (radius_ratio 0.06; veterans 1.35x). Long-lived (300-500+ years). It needs deep alluvial soil with groundwater in reach, so around Placerville and Shingle Springs it stands on valley floors, swales and the lower slopes, mostly below about 600 m, with blue oak on the drier slopes above. Decurrent Rauh's model like the other oaks: a short, massive trunk (trunk.length_ratio 0.32) forking into a few heavy scaffold limbs (split_prob 0.5) that spread wide and arch down (level-1 droop_deg 28), with long pendulous outer branchlets (level-2 tropism -0.06, droop_deg 16): the drooping skirt that sets valley oak apart from blue oak at a glance, strongest in veterans (droop_deg 40). Open-grown crowns in the photographs are 1.3-1.8 times as wide as tall with the crown base at 0.06-0.12 of the height. Bark grey, thick, deeply furrowed into small rectangular blocks ('platy' with small plates, 8-14 cm; it is checkered more coarsely and darker than blue oak's). Leaves 5-10 cm, deeply cut into 7-11 rounded lobes, dark green above and paler, finely hairy below: leaf_shape lobed_large (2026-10-26, was oblong_wavy, which does not read lobe_depth) with 9 round-tipped pinnate lobes cut 0.55 of the way in (lobes, lobe_depth, lobe_tip round, lobe_style pinnate) at leaf_size_m 0.08, and a paler palette tint for the undersides. Deciduous: leafs out in March, holds its leaves into November or December, yellow-brown in fall (leaf_on.fall 0.75), bare in winter with fine pendulous twigs (winter_twigs). Oak mistletoe (Phoradendron) is common in valley oak crowns (mistletoe prob 0.5, veterans 0.8). Acorns: yes, for the acorn game. Long and slender (3-5 cm), ripening in one season and dropping September-November; scrub-jays and ground squirrels cache them.
